text:
kevin: pager — SCIM deprovision errors spiked to ~20% at 02:10 UTC, majority 403/KMS AccessDenied and a few mismatched NameID lookups in audit. Anyone touch SAML mapping or KMS keys overnight?
anya: i rotated the organisation SAML NameID format in the mapping PR last night (persistent->email). that might change which extId SCIM looks up. i also triggered a scheduled KMS key rotation for extid-encrypt-key at 01:40 UTC (per rotation window).
matt: whoa two changes close together. can you paste the exact error from the provisioner?
kevin: logs show both decrypt denies and some "extid not found" errors. snippet: 
```
2026-09-12T02:09:58Z ERROR scim-provisioner deprov.go:132 "failed to decrypt external_id" err="AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:666777888999:key/ccbb-a1b2"
2026-09-12T02:10:01Z WARN scim-provisioner lookup.go:78 "extid lookup mismatch" user=svcacc-12 expected_nameid=persistent actual_nameid=email
```
anya: hm the NameID change explains the lookup mismatches (SCIM attempted deprov for a different extId). the KMS AccessDenied indicates the rotating key's policy didn't include the new provisioner principal or the alias mapping changed and we tried wrong key id. i forgot to include the rotated role in the new key grants when we rekeyed.
matt: so combined failure: some deprovs targeted the wrong extId due to NameID format change and other deprovs failed to decrypt because the new key policy omitted the SCIM role. explains orphaned accounts.
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-8691 "SCIM deprov failures after SAML NameID format change + KMS rotation" 02:12 UTC 02:25 paging eng-platform & eng-security
kms-ops-bot: KMS rotation completed at 2026-09-12T01:40Z -> new key id ccbb-a1b2; key policy currently allows principals: arn:aws:iam::666777888999:role/scim-provisioner-v1 (old) only.
kevin: proposed immediate remediation: 1) add current provisioner role(s) to new key policy allow list 2) temporarily revert NameID mapping in staging to validate backfill logic 3) restart scim-provisioner pods to clear cached KMS contexts 4) run controlled backfill for 01:30-02:12 window.
matt: adding condition to key policy (aws:PrincipalArn) and keeping old role for 48h grace. also add alias mapping back if any aliases pointed to old key id.
anya: applied key policy update at 02:18 UTC and verified both scim roles present in policy; added Condition on aws:PrincipalAccount.
kms-ops-bot: key policy updated (change-id kp-2026-486) at 2026-09-12T02:18:23Z
matt: restarting deployment: kubectl -n idp rollout restart deployment/scim-provisioner
oncall-bot: k8s: deployment/scim-provisioner restarted (rolling) 02:20 UTC
kevin: backfill run: tools/scim backfill --since 2026-09-12T01:30Z --until 2026-09-12T02:12Z --batch 150 -> first batch shows previously failed items now decrypting and deprovisioning successfully.
anya: follow-ups created: - eng-platform: add pre-rotation checklist that includes updating key policies and verifying alias->key mappings - eng-security: add test that simulates NameID format change + rekey to staging CI - ops: add alert for simultaneous KMS AccessDenied spikes + high extid-lookup-mismatch rate - docs: update RBAC rename/runbook to include KMS and SAML mapping steps
matt: filed GH-6249 with checklist and links to incident. oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-8691 resolved -> root cause: SAML NameID format change combined with KMS rotation where new key policy omitted provisioner principal; remediation: updated key policy, restarted provisioner, ran backfill, follow-ups opened.
kevin: good catch. can we add a gate in the SAML mapping deploy pipeline to fail if any pending key rotations/alias changes are scheduled?
anya: yes will add to eng-platform backlog. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
